Murray Plastics works with numerous plastic materials, including eco-friendly options, and assists customers with material selection for each project.

Murray Plastics says its differentiator is personable, down-to-earth service that comes from founder-led ownership, along with in-house mold building and engineering support that helps clients improve product designs. name: Musco Sports Lighting, LLC
old_description: Since 2023, Bullitt County Public Schools has standardized the lighting performance across its athletic facilities at North, Central, and East High Schools. They’ve invested in Musco LED systems for football, baseball, softball, and tennis, with tailored solutions for new installations and retrofit applications. Additionally, each football stadium now features color-changing luminaires and Show-Light® entertainment technology.
about:
Musco Sports Lighting, LLC is headquartered in Oskaloosa, Iowa. For over half a century, the company has developed sports and large-area lighting systems, growing from its Iowa roots into a global provider of facility solutions.

The company designs and manufactures LED lighting systems for sports venues and large-area applications. Its product portfolio includes the Light-Structure System™, 5 Easy Pieces™ packaged solutions, Mini-Pitch System™ modular fields, Show-Light® color-changing luminaires with entertainment technology, and the Control-Link® remote monitoring and control service. Musco provides custom design, project management, installation support, and 24/7 proactive system monitoring through a team of more than 2,100 employees worldwide.

Musco serves K-12 school districts such as Bullitt County Public Schools, universities including the University of Idaho, municipal parks departments like Windsor Parks and Recreation in Colorado, professional sports organizations including Blackpool FC in England and the Gaelic Athletic Association at Croke Park in Ireland, and international venues such as Mission Whitten Oval in Australia. The company was also named the Official Sport Presentation and Broadcast Lighting Provider for the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

Musco emphasizes responsible lighting that minimizes spill light and glare, citing DarkSky certification achievements on projects. Its founding principle centers on existing for the benefit of the team, which the company says drives long-tenured careers and a focus on making high-performance lighting affordable while expanding recreational opportunities in communities.

name: Myriad Semiconductor Manufacturing Division
old_description: Our business concept is based upon building long-term, mutually beneficial business relationships. Our success in achieving our stated goals is best measured by our longevitiy.  Since 1983 Myriad has proven its desire and ability to meet the ever-changing expectations of our diverse industry.
about:
Myriad Semiconductor Manufacturing Division is based in Garfield, Arkansas, and has operated since 1983. The company is owned by Bobby Hobbs, who is identified as the owner on the company’s website. Founded over four decades ago, the business was built around serving the semiconductor equipment market with a focus on long-term customer relationships.

The company designs and supplies custom-configured mask aligners for production, research and development, and university teaching environments. It also remanufactures existing Kasper and Quintel mask aligners to extend equipment life. Myriad maintains a large inventory of spare parts for semiconductor processing equipment and provides printed circuit board repair, field service, and training. In addition, the company stocks a variety of electronic, electrical, and mechanical components — including integrated circuits, transistors, capacitors, sensors, and switches — which it sells through an eBay storefront called Myriad Surplus Store.

Myriad serves semiconductor manufacturers, university laboratories, and R&D facilities worldwide. Its mask aligners are used in production lines, research settings, and teaching programs, though specific customer names are not disclosed.

The company states that its business concept centers on building long-term, mutually beneficial relationships and measures success by its longevity.

about:
NAS Electronics operates from Henderson, Nevada, after originating as an idea in the hills of California. The company has been active in electronics manufacturing for over thirty years, though a specific founding year is not disclosed. Ownership structure and founder names are not publicly stated.

The shop provides end-to-end electronics manufacturing services including PCB assembly (both turnkey and consignment), final box-build assembly, cable and wire harness assembly, and design-for-manufacturability (DFM) review. NAS Electronics positions itself on end-to-end expertise, strong supplier relationships, state-of-the-art facilities, and extensive industry knowledge that aim to expand client capabilities without overhead. A U.S.-based team and a willingness to go the extra mile — such as executive travel to prevent line-down situations — are highlighted as service differentiators.

name: NOLA Steele Fabrication and Erection
old_description: With more than 20 years in the industry, President Karen L. Williams founded NOLA Steele Fabrication and Erection LLC in 2014.
about:
NOLA Steele Fabrication and Erection LLC was founded in 2014 by Karen L. Williams in Harvey, Louisiana. Williams brought more than 20 years of industry experience to the venture, establishing the company as a woman-owned and service-disabled veteran-owned small business with additional certifications as a minority-owned, economically disadvantaged women-owned, and 8(a) firm.

The company provides structural steel erection, custom steel fabrication (including design, stairs, additions, alterations, maintenance, and repairs), skilled labor supply (welders, fitters, riggers, tackers, ironworkers, painters, and sandblasters), miscellaneous steel work such as handrails, guardrails, and balconies, stair stringer fabrication and installation, repair welding, steel supply, and limited steel demolition. It operates with a team of 35 trained professionals and has completed over 500 projects since inception.

NOLA Steele serves the construction sector, supporting new commercial and industrial construction, renovation, and repair projects. Its certifications position it for government and public-sector work, and its client base includes general contractors, developers, and agencies requiring certified small-business participation.

The firm emphasizes a thorough quality-control program and adherence to high safety standards, aiming to exceed project criteria for excellence and customer satisfaction. Its track record of 20-plus years of experience, 500-plus completed projects, and a certified workforce are cited as key differentiators.

about:
NXP Semiconductors USA maintains its U.S. headquarters in Allen, Texas, anchoring the company's significant domestic operations. The business was founded in 2006 after the spin-off of Philips Semiconductors, creating an independent global semiconductor supplier with a strong presence in the United States.

NXP designs and manufactures semiconductor devices such as microcontrollers, RFID chips, and automotive integrated circuits. The company employs over 15,000 people worldwide and operates extensive design, manufacturing, and test capabilities to support high-volume production for automotive, industrial, and IoT applications.

The company serves customers in the automotive, industrial, IoT, and mobile sectors. Its products are integrated into vehicle electronics, secure identification systems, industrial automation equipment, and mobile devices, addressing requirements for performance, security, and connectivity.

NXP differentiates itself through a focus on secure connectivity, offering automotive-grade microcontrollers and secure identification ICs that meet stringent safety and security standards for modern electronic systems.

name: Nashville Electric Service - Music City Solar
old_description: The city spoke. We listened. Thanks to the voice of our customers, what once was a landfill off I-65 is now the site of Nashville's first community solar park that includes 17,020 panels, available to participating customers, marking an important step in offering clean, efficient, maintenance-free energy.
about:
Music City Solar operates from Madison, Tennessee, as a program of Nashville Electric Service (NES), a public utility. The initiative launched on August 1, 2018, when the utility transformed a former landfill off I-65 into Nashville's first community solar park. The project began after customers expressed demand for renewable energy options, prompting NES to develop a shared solar facility that would allow broad participation without rooftop installations.

The program manages a 17,020-panel solar array that feeds clean energy directly into the NES grid. Customers purchase subscriptions to individual panels and receive a monthly solar credit on their electric bills through 2038. As of the latest data, 3,142 panels are leased to customers, generating over 21 million kilowatt-hours to date. The park also reserves panels for the Solar Angel Fund, a donation-based component that provides energy assistance to low-income households; 1,015 panels have been donated so far, with 12,863 panels still available for new subscribers.

The service targets residential customers — both homeowners and renters — across the NES service territory who want renewable energy without upfront installation costs or maintenance. It also serves low-income households through the Solar Angel donation channel, administered in partnership with The Community Foundation of Middle Tennessee. Commercial or industrial participation is not described in the available materials.

NES frames the program as a direct response to customer voice: "The city spoke. We listened." The utility emphasizes maintenance-free participation, long-term bill credits, and a community-focused model that combines environmental impact with local energy assistance. The park's location on a reclaimed landfill underscores a dual benefit of land reuse and emissions reduction.

old_description: Our National Food NW farms have provided the local community with the highest quality fresh eggs for over 60 years. Our values guide our everyday decisions — environmental sustainability, humane animal care, and strong stewardship in our community. Our team of dedicated employees work diligently every day to ensure that you have fresh eggs on your family’s table or for your food service needs.
about:
National Foods NW operates from Lind, Washington, with a business address in Everett, and has supplied the Pacific Northwest with fresh eggs for more than six decades. The company runs its own farms under the National Food NW banner and markets a specialty line under the Cherry Lane Family Farms name.

The operation produces shell eggs in several varieties—organic, cage-free brown and white, and omega-3 enriched—and runs a liquid‑egg processing line branded as Chef’s Select® for food‑service and manufacturing customers. The farms completed a full conversion to 100 % cage‑free production across Washington in 2024.

Customers include regional grocery retailers, food‑service distributors, and manufacturers that incorporate egg ingredients into prepared foods. The company emphasizes local delivery to family tables and commercial kitchens throughout the Pacific Northwest.

The business states that its decisions are guided by three pillars: environmental sustainability, humane animal care, and community stewardship. The cage‑free transition is cited as a direct outcome of those values.

name: National Molding
old_description: Global Manufacturer of Precision Engineered Plastic Components
about:
National Molding, headquartered in Miami Lakes, Florida, was founded in 1982. The company began as an injection molding specialist and developed proprietary Hetero Cavity technology that remains central to its operations today.

The company produces over 3.5 billion parts annually using highly engineered resins. Its capabilities span precision injection molding, medical product molding, metal-to-plastic conversions, low-cost modular molding, pre- and post-molding services, design for manufacturability, tooling design and manufacturing, cleanroom molding, insert over molding, and a full-service tool room with CNC machining. Molding machines range from 40 to 300 tons, supported by automation and assembly equipment. National Molding operates plants in the United States, Canada, and China, and over 80 percent of its output relies on the in-house Hetero Cavity process.

Automotive customers — Tier 1, Tier 2, and direct OEMs — account for more than 60 percent of revenue. The medical division, certified to ISO 13485 and FDA registered, serves healthcare, life science, dental, and diagnostic markets from an ISO Class 8 cleanroom. Commercial lines cover plumbing fixtures, telecommunications, appliances, irrigation, furniture, marine, and electrical products. The DuraflexUSA division supplies Berry Amendment–compliant buckles and fasteners to sporting goods, military, tactical, and pet-supply markets, while a separate line produces tactical body armor release systems for military and law enforcement.

National Molding differentiates itself through its proprietary Hetero Cavity injection molding technology, developed internally and used across the majority of its parts. The company also offers full consulting and rapid-response contract engineering services, and maintains ISO 9001, ISO 13485, and IATF 16949 certifications across its operations.
